scenes.say: Ever had two Python packages fight over which version of a library to use? How can you keep your project stable?

scenes.label: Conflict
scenes.sub: When packages need incompatible versions of the same dependency.
scenes.say: A dependency conflict happens when different packages need different versions of the same library. Python can't satisfy both at once.
Pinning means locking dependencies to exact versions. Without it, installs can change over time and break your code. With pinning, your builds stay stable and predictable.

scenes.title: Pinned Dependencies
scenes.say: Here's what pinning looks like in a requirements file. Each package has a specific version, so nothing changes unless you decide to update.

scenes.question: How do you avoid dependency conflicts?
scenes.right: Pin exact versions and use lock files to avoid conflicts.
scenes.say: In interviews, don't just say you install the latest versions. The real answer is to pin exact versions and use lock files to keep things conflict-free.
